blocks.title: What is kinematics?
blocks.summary: Kinematics describes motion without explaining its causes. Position tells us where something is relative to a reference. Velocity tells us how fast position changes and in what direction. Acceleration means velocity is changing: speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction—even at a constant speed.

options.feedback: Velocity includes direction. Changing direction is acceleration even with constant speed.

options.text: No, because its speed stays constant.
options.feedback: Constant speed is only part of constant velocity. The direction is changing.

options.text: Only if it starts moving faster.
options.feedback: Acceleration includes speeding up, slowing down, and changing direction.

blocks.title: Position & displacement on a number line
blocks.summary: Position is a location relative to a chosen origin. In this lesson, right is positive. Displacement is final position minus initial position: $\Delta x=x_f-x_i$. Distance adds the lengths of all parts of a journey. A negative displacement tells you a direction; it is not a negative distance.

blocks.markdown:
**Position** describes a location. **Displacement** describes a change in location.

A **scalar** has magnitude only: distance is a scalar. A **vector** has magnitude and direction: displacement is a vector. In one dimension, the sign tells you the direction.

question.prompt: A cart returns to where it started. Which statement must be true?

options.feedback: Displacement compares final and initial position. The path can still have a nonzero length.
Distance adds the lengths traveled. Returning does not erase the outward trip.

options.text: Its distance is negative on the return trip.
options.feedback: Distance is a nonnegative length. A direction can make displacement negative, not distance.

blocks.title: Distance and displacement method

**Problem:** Name the quantities you need.
